root_idea.summary: A semantic field of going to an extreme or being worn down, extending to insistent inquiry, exceptional attentiveness, and thorough knowledge.
root_idea.development: The supplied lexical discussion links pressing inquiry to making a hoof worn through travel, and also records related extensions such as close trimming, attentive kindness, and knowing thoroughly.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَحْفَى rather than the inflected Quranic imperfect يُحْفِ.
Displayed as the adjective حَفِيّ, the citation form corresponding to the Quranic inflections.

senses.definition: To press or importune someone in asking, demanding, or seeking information.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the subject presses the addressee in a demand; the same lexical use includes persistent questioning and insistence in seeking an answer.

senses.definition: Exceptionally kind, gracious, and benevolently attentive toward someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ for the person receiving the kindness; the Quranic occurrence in 19:47 describes gracious and considerate treatment.

senses.definition: Thoroughly knowing or well informed about something.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence in 7:187 uses the adjective for being fully informed; this is distinct from its gracious-treatment use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become barefoot, without sandals or boots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I bodily use, describing the loss or absence of footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Barefootedness: the state of being without sandals or boots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with the Form I use of becoming or being barefoot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a foot or hoof, to become attenuated, chafed, abraded, or worn through walking, treading, or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to human feet and to the hooves of camels, horses, and similar animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive or treat someone with marked honour, kindness, affection, gentleness, solicitude, and joy; to take pains over his needs and inquire carefully into his condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I construction expressing unusually attentive and warm treatment, including especially careful greeting or inquiry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the usual bounds in an injunction, charge, or urging directed to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes a person toward whom the excessive injunction or charge is directed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To honour someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I transitive construction distinct from حَفِيَ بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give something to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deny or refuse someone, or to withhold good from him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported contrary meaning of the same transitive form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dispute with someone in words, vehemently or obstinately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or adversarial verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, to become attenuated, chafed, or abraded in the hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use describing the resulting condition of the animal's hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone barefoot or make his feet bare of sandals or boots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use concerning footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wear down or abrade a person's foot or an animal's hoof through much walking, treading, or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use describing physical wear of the sole or hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clip the moustache very closely or to the utmost degree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV grooming use expressing extreme closeness or thoroughness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To examine a horse's teeth thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use of carrying an examination to the utmost degree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge someone to investigate news or information thoroughly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use in which one incites another to inquire or investigate to the utmost.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To despise someone or bring a fault-imputation against him so as to involve him in confusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV hostile or disparaging construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive or labour earnestly in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V use expressing exertion in a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To practise an artifice or contrivance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported Form V use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For each of two parties to bring a complaint against the other before a ruler, who refers the case to a judge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI reciprocal legal construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pull up short or scant herbs from the ground, or to uproot something completely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII use associated with removing vegetation by the fingertips or extirpating it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people or animals to consume a pasture so completely that none of its herbage remains.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form VIII use describing exhaustive grazing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or inquire after news or tidings beyond the usual bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X use expressing excessive persistence in seeking information.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a foot or hoof attenuated, chafed, abraded, or worn through walking, treading, or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of a person, camel, horse, or similar animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of being barefoot, without sandals or boots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One of the simple nouns used for barefootedness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of having a foot or hoof attenuated, chafed, abraded, or worn through walking or travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This secondary nominal attribution is lexicographically qualified in the supplied evidence and may properly belong to a verbal noun instead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Excessively attentive or importunate in asking or inquiring about another's condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical adjectival use focused on persistent inquiry, distinct from the Quranic senses of graciousness and full knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Walking barefoot, without sandals or boots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial adjective; its plural is reported as حُفَاةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A judge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical use synonymous with قَاضٍ.
